chapters.title: Introduction
chapters.html:
The real estate market moves in cycles: periods that favour sellers, periods that favour buyers, and transitions in between. Understanding these dynamics in Greater Montreal helps you decide with discernment rather than following the crowd's emotions.

This guide explains the phases of the market, the indicators to watch, and how to act according to the context — without trying to perfectly “time” the market.

Informational content. Each chapter ends with a lined “My Notes” page.

chapters.title: Buyer's Market, Seller's Market
chapters.objective: Recognizing which type of market you're in.
chapters.html:
Recognizing which type of market you're in.

In a seller's market, demand exceeds supply: few properties, quick sales, and possible bidding wars. In a buyer's market, supply exceeds demand: more choice, longer timelines, and downward negotiation. Between the two lies a balanced market.

  • Key indicator: the number of months of inventory (how long it would take to sell off the properties on the market).
  • Average time on market and sold price / asking price ratio.
  • These dynamics vary by area and property type.
Émilie's tip

Adapt your strategy to the type of market. In a seller's market, you offer quickly and cleanly; in a buyer's market, you take your time and negotiate. The same behaviour doesn't work in both.

chapters.title: The Factors That Move the Market
chapters.html:
Understanding the forces at play.

  • Interest rates: they strongly influence borrowing capacity and demand.
  • Economy and employment: confidence, incomes, migration.
  • Supply: housing starts, land availability, regulation.
  • Demographics and neighbourhoods: some areas stay sought-after regardless of the cycle.

No single factor tells the whole story; it's their combination that shapes the market.

Émilie's tip

Watch interest rates above all: they're the most powerful short-term lever on demand and therefore on prices. But never base a life decision on a single variable.

chapters.title: Acting Without Trying to Guess the Peak
chapters.objective: Deciding based on your needs, not on speculation.
chapters.html:
Deciding based on your needs, not on speculation.

No one perfectly “times” the market. For most households, the right decision depends mainly on their personal situation (need, stability, capacity) and their time horizon, rather than on an attempt to predict the peak or the trough.

Real estate generally rewards patience and long-term holding, which smooth out the cycles.

Émilie's tip

Don't wait indefinitely for “the perfect moment”: it's only recognizable in hindsight. A good property bought for the right reasons, with a long horizon, rides out the cycles.

chapters.title: Action Plan
chapters.html:
Your next steps, in concrete terms.

This week

  1. Identify the current type of market in my area.
  2. Track inventory, timelines, and the sold/asking price ratio.

Within 30 days

  1. Understand the effect of rates on my project.
  2. Clarify my needs and my time horizon.

After that

  1. Decide based on my situation, with Émilie's insight into the local market.

  • Long-term horizon: holding that smooths out the cycles.
